answer: An agent network curbs Sybil attacks using solar occultation timing. Physical nodes prove unique presence by timestamping sunlight cutoffs as the solar disk crosses the terrain horizon, cross-validated between stations on an open dune and a ridge summit. An attacker incurs steep capital and siting costs maintaining discrete photometer rigs rather than cloning software threads. However, localized cloud cover attenuates optical signals, occasionally rejecting honest participants.
